scenes.tts: The film's tree and your simulation both gave each kind its own zone by rule. Did real warblers use spruce trees in different patterns? To find out, keep the same tree and replace imagined paths with recorded observations.
scenes.narration: The film's tree and your simulation both gave each kind its own zone by rule. Did real warblers use spruce trees in different patterns? To find out, keep the same tree and replace imagined paths with recorded observations.
scenes.visual: Reuse the first film's large schematic spruce and exact color map: habitat GOLD; insects YELLOW; Cape May TEAL; Blackburnian ORANGE; black-throated green GREEN; bay-breasted PURPLE; myrtle RED. The colored model paths dissolve. A stopwatch, clipboard, and pale grid move into their places. Show the study years on screen only.
Keep branches swaying gently. The title 'Reading the Warblers' Tree Map' appears briefly. Its underline transforms into the top edge of the observation grid.

scenes.tts: Robert MacArthur divided spruce trees into named zones. Height bands ran down from the treetop. Each branch also had a base, a middle, and outer tips. Using the same map for every bird made their patterns comparable.
scenes.narration: Robert MacArthur divided spruce trees into named zones. Height bands ran down from the treetop. Each branch also had a base, a middle, and outer tips. Using the same map for every bird made their patterns comparable.
scenes.visual: Horizontal bands sweep down the tree from its top. A branch enlarges inside a circular inset. Its base, middle, and outer tips highlight in order. Labels appear only after each region settles. The inset folds back into the same tree, leaving a clean grid.

scenes.tts: When MacArthur could see a bird, he timed how long it stayed in each zone. The forest was dense, and birds were often hidden. Many hours of watching produced few useful seconds. Each colored timer fills only while its bird remains visible.
scenes.narration: When MacArthur could see a bird, he timed how long it stayed in each zone. The forest was dense, and birds were often hidden. Many hours of watching produced few useful seconds. Each colored timer fills only while its bird remains visible.
scenes.visual: One colored bird moves through the gridded tree. Its timer fills while visible, stops behind dense needles, then resumes after it emerges. Recorded ticks fly from the stopwatch into the matching zone. Repeat rapidly with the other colors while the tree remains fixed.

scenes.tts: For each kind, the recorded seconds became percentages of its total recorded time. Darker zones mean more time there. The maps show different centers of activity, but their colored areas still overlap. No bird owns a private slice of the tree. Some kinds centered activity high in the tree. Others centered lower, or spread their time more widely.

scenes.visual: The stopwatch ticks transform into filled zone cells. On-screen percentage labels grow from the computed table values; do not speak them. Duplicate the same tree outline into five aligned strips, one per color. Dark zones pulse at each kind's center, while shared zones crossfade to show overlap. Label the display 'RECORDED TIME'.

scenes.tts: Predict how to read a shared zone. Both kinds clearly have recorded time there. Does that show complete separation, or does it show overlap? Hold your answer while both cells glow.
scenes.narration: Predict how to read a shared zone. Both kinds clearly have recorded time there. Does that show complete separation, or does it show overlap? Hold your answer while both cells glow.
scenes.visual: Collapse the five strips into two rows from the lesson table. Enlarge one shared zone with both printed values on screen. Outline both nonzero cells in their bird colors. Show the two answer labels 'SEPARATION' and 'OVERLAP' without selecting either.
Keep both nonzero cells glowing and both answer labels neutral. A small thinking ring fills once. No check mark or reveal appears.

scenes.tts: It shows overlap. Both kinds spent recorded time in that zone. Their percentages can still differ, so overlap does not mean identical use. Read down a column to compare kinds, then read across a row to find each kind's pattern. A large value marks a strong center of activity. Smaller values still matter because they show shared use.
scenes.narration: It shows overlap. Both kinds spent recorded time in that zone. Their percentages can still differ, so overlap does not mean identical use. Read down a column to compare kinds, then read across a row to find each kind's pattern. A large value marks a strong center of activity. Smaller values still matter because they show shared use.
scenes.visual: Select 'OVERLAP'. A vertical gold guide moves down the chosen column, then turns and travels across each colored row. Transform the two rows back into tree strips. Their highlighted regions partly cover one another while their darkest cells remain different.

scenes.tts: Now separate observation from explanation. The table records time, not insects eaten. Some records were singing birds, not feeding birds. Visibility matters because dense branches can hide birds. Percentages summarize what the observer could record, not everything birds did. The study did not directly measure competition. Different tree use may reduce competition, but the table alone cannot prove that cause.

scenes.visual: Place three large evidence cards beside the tree: 'TIME RECORDED', 'SOME SINGING', and 'NO COMPETITION MEASURE'. A crossed-out food counter appears only when 'not insects eaten' is spoken. Then connect the observed pattern to a dotted arrow labelled 'may reduce competition', marked 'INFERENCE'.

scenes.tts: A careful claim keeps those parts apart. The warblers shared a habitat and used it in different, overlapping patterns. That pattern carefully supports a possible explanation for sharing. It remains evidence for the idea, not proof of every step.

scenes.visual: Arrange three connected blocks across the frame: 'OBSERVATION' above colored overlapping maps, 'INFERENCE' above a dotted competition arrow, and 'LIMIT' above the stopwatch. The blocks settle into a claim-evidence-reasoning chain. Fade all but the final tree before the end card.
One line only, centered in large type: 'Different niches can reduce competition, helping species share a habitat.' No title, subtitle, logo, or smaller line.
